title: Stable modification of a flat multipointed relative curve
statement: Let $S$ be an excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] scheme with generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $\eta$. Let $C\to S$ and $H\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$, respectively, and let $i:H\hookrightarrow C$ be a closed immersion. The scheme $H$ may be empty; neither morphism is assumed proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $C_\eta$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $H_\eta$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $\kappa(\eta)$. There exist an excellent integral Noetherian scheme $S'$ and a projective dominant generically finite morphism $r:S'\to S$ in the finite-projective-space sense [def-kun-projective], and a commutative morphism of closed pairs $(m,n):(C',H')\to(C,H)\times_S S'$, such that $m$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] and $n$ is proper, and both induce isomorphisms on the generic fibres over $S'$. The morphism $C'\to S'$ is flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with at-worst-nodal geometric fibres; $H'\hookrightarrow C'$ is closed, $H'\to S'$ is etale, and $H'$ is contained in the relative smooth locus. Here at-worst-nodal means that every singular point of a geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$. Generically finite means finite over a dense open of the target. The generic extension and the degree of $r$ are not required to have degree prime to any integer.

source.place: Exposé X, §3.2.2 and proof of Theorem 3.4, Steps 3 and first sentence of Step 4, printed pp. 158, 160--161: stable modification, then projective alteration refinement (no Sylow or prime-to-l conclusion is used). The input is Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 (existence), 1.1 (projectivity), and §1.2 (multipointed curves and eta-modifications). A projective Chow refinement of the alteration gives finite-projective-space projectivity of r.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-temkin-stable-modification] to $(C,H)\to S$. The hypotheses of a multipointed curve are precisely the two flat finitely presented maps of pure relative dimensions $1,0$ and the closed immersion. The smooth generic curve with etale marking in its smooth locus is semistable. We obtain an integral excellent Noetherian $\widetilde S$, a proper dominant generically finite $a:\widetilde S\to S$, a proper projective-bundle modification $b:\widetilde C\to C\times_S\widetilde S$, and a closed marking $\widetilde H\subset\widetilde C$. In particular the cited statement supplies a map $d:\widetilde H\to H\times_S\widetilde S$ commuting with $b$, and both $b$ and $d$ induce isomorphisms on generic fibres. It also supplies the semistable multipointed family and its preservation by base change. Neither properness nor separatedness of $C\to S$ is needed.

source.place: Exposé X §3.2.2 and Theorem 3.4 Step 3, printed pp. 158, 160; Temkin §1.2 and Theorems 1.5, 1.1 (source URL read online).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] to $a:\widetilde S\to S$: properness includes separatedness and finite type. Obtain a proper surjection $\pi:T\to\widetilde S$, an $S$-immersion $j:T\to\mathbf P^N_S$, and a dense open $V\subset\widetilde S$ such that $W:=\pi^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a), $T\to S$ is proper, so $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Thus every open of $T$ is quasi-compact, and $W\hookrightarrow T$ is a quasi-compact immersion. Define $S'$ as its scheme-theoretic image. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] this is a closed subscheme of $T$ with ideal the kernel of restriction to $W$; by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], $W\to S'$ is an open immersion with topologically and scheme-theoretically dense image. We identify it with $W$. This construction does not require $W$ to be dense in $T$.

source.place: Tag 0200, label lemma-chow-Noetherian; morphisms.tex Tag 01R8, label lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image. The image construction discards components outside the isomorphism open.

proof.text: The scheme $S'$ is integral. Indeed, $W\simeq V$ is a nonempty integral open and is dense in $S'$ by the preceding step. Thus $S'$ is irreducible. For an affine open $A=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$ meeting $S'$, write $I=\ker(R\to\Gamma(A\cap W,\mathcal O_W))$. The kernel formula in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel](1) identifies $S'\cap A$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. Density ensures $A\cap W\ne\varnothing$. Sections on this nonempty open of an integral scheme inject into its function field, so $\Gamma(A\cap W,\mathcal O_W)$ is a domain. Hence its subring $R/I$ is a domain. These affine opens cover $S'$, proving reducedness and integrality as in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Put $q=\pi|_{S'}:S'\to\widetilde S$. Since $\pi^{-1}(V)=W$ and $W\subset S'$, the restriction $q^{-1}(V)\to V$ is the original isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01R8, label lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, kernel description; elementary domain and density argument.

proof.text: Let $r=a\circ q:S'\to S$. The closed immersion $S'\hookrightarrow T$ is proper, and composition with the proper $\pi$ and $a$ makes $r$ proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(c). The composite $j':S'\hookrightarrow T\xrightarrow{j}\mathbf P^N_S$ is an immersion by its part (e). The projection $\mathbf P^N_S\to S$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated. Since $r$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $j'$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes it a closed immersion. Consequently $r$ is projective in the finite-projective-space sense [def-kun-projective]. Properness gives finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $S'$ Noetherian; on affine charts its finite-type coordinate algebras over excellent affine charts of $S$ are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Thus $S'$ is excellent as well.

source.place: Tags 01W3, 01W5 (proper composition and closed immersions), 01W6 label lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed; schemes.tex Tag 01IQ label lemma-immersion-when-closed. Projective space properness and excellence as in the cited nodes.

proof.text: The map $r$ is dominant and finite over a dense open. To see the latter explicitly, choose a dense open $U\subset S$ over which $a$ is finite. Since $\widetilde S$ is integral and $a$ is dominant, the finite generic fibre is the spectrum of a finite domain over $\kappa(\eta)$, hence a field: $a^{-1}(\eta)=\{\widetilde\eta\}$. The dense open $V$ contains $\widetilde\eta$. Properness means that $a$ is a closed map [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $F:=a(\widetilde S\setminus V)$ is closed and avoids $\eta$. Over $U_0:=U\setminus F$, all of $a^{-1}(U_0)$ lies in $V$ and $q$ is an isomorphism. Thus $r|_{r^{-1}(U_0)}$ identifies with the finite map $a|_{a^{-1}(U_0)}$. Moreover $q$ contains $V$ in its image and is dominant, and the generic point maps to $\eta$, so $r$ is dominant. Thus $r$ is finite over a dense open, as required.

source.place: Theorem 3.4 Steps 3--4: alteration refinement. The dense-open finiteness verification is written here from the definition of properness and the finite generic fibre.

proof.text: Form $C'=\widetilde C\times_{\widetilde S}S'$ and $H'=\widetilde H\times_{\widetilde S}S'$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Base-changing $b,d$ along $q$ gives a morphism of closed pairs $(m,n)$ to $(C,H)\times_SS'$. The base-change clause of [lem-trf-temkin-stable-modification] gives the flat finitely presented pure-dimensional nodal curve, with etale closed marking in its relative smooth locus. To verify projective-bundle projectivity, write $b$ as a closed immersion into $\operatorname{Proj}_B(\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E)$ for $B=C\times_S\widetilde S$, as in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Pull back to $B'=C\times_SS'$. By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary], this Proj pulls back to $\operatorname{Proj}_{B'}(g^*\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E)$. The symmetric algebra on $g^*\mathcal E$ is $g^*\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E$: both represent linear maps from $g^*\mathcal E$ into a commutative algebra. Finite generators of $\mathcal E$ pull back to finite generators. The closed immersion pulls back by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). This is the required projective-bundle factorization of $m$; the same part makes $m$ proper because $b$ is proper. As $q$ is an isomorphism over $V$, it identifies the generic point of $S'$ with that of $\widetilde S$. The generic-fibre isomorphisms of both $b$ and $d$ therefore give the claimed generic-fibre isomorphisms of $m$ and $n:H'\to H\times_SS'$.

source.place: Exposé X §3.2.2 and Theorem 3.4 Step 3 and first sentence of Step 4; relative Proj base-change comparison and closed-immersion base change as in the cited nodes. Relative Proj comparison: Stacks Tag 01O3, constructions.tex, label lemma-relative-proj-base-change; closed immersions: Tag 01QR, morphisms.tex, label lemma-base-change-closed-immersion.

proof.text: Finally $n$ is proper. Put $B'=C\times_SS'$ and $K=C'\times_{B'}(H\times_SS')$. Since $m$ is proper, $K\to H\times_SS'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). The morphism of pairs gives $H'\to K$; it is a closed immersion. Indeed, locally in $C'$, let $I$ be the ideal of $H'$ and $J$ that of $K$. The factorization says $J\subseteq I$, and the map $\mathcal O_{C'}/J\to\mathcal O_{C'}/I$ is surjective, giving the assertion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Parts (a),(c) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] now make the composite $n$ proper. The completed geometric-fibre local equation supplied by the Temkin node is exactly the at-worst-nodal condition in the item, and its smooth-locus marking gives the last condition. No degree condition was imposed, and the construction also covers the empty marking.
